"Set-aside the Order dated 31.10.2023 on I.A.filed under Order 7 Rule 11(a) & (d) in O.S.No.430/2020 passed by the learned II Addl. Civil Judge and JMFC., at Devanahalli, this revision petition be allowed in ends of justice."

sentences.text: 3. Accepting the reasons, IA-1/2023 is allowed.
Legal representatives names therein are permitted to prosecute the petition.

4. The Suit in O.S. No.430/2020 had been filed by respondent No.1 seeking for the following reliefs:
a) To pass a Judgement and Decree against the defendant for permanent injunction restraining the defendants without due course of law, their agents, servants,
subordinates and henchmen in interfering with peaceful Possession and enjoyment in respect of the plaint schedule property.
b) To pass such other relief/s as the Hon'ble Court may deem fit to grant under the circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice and equity.

In the said suit, defendant No.1 had filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11 (a & d) of CPC for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the land, subject matter of the said suit for bare injunction had been acquired under the provisions of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 ['KIAD Act' for short.

entities.text: Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 ['KIAD Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Preliminary notification having been issued under Subsection (1) of Section 28, final notification having been issued under Subsection (4) of Section 28, the possession of the said property is deemed to be vested with the State.
An award having been passed, compensation has been collected by the plaintiff and as such, there is nothing which would survive for consideration.
The land having been acquired, the plaintiff would have no subsisting right, title or interest in the said property, let alone seek for an order of injunction.

6. The said application having been opposed, the trial Court vide the impugned order dated 31.10.2023 dismissed the said application on the ground that the NC: 2024:KHC:21183 consideration of an application under Order 7 Rule 11 has to be made only on the basis of the averments made in the plaint and most of the submissions made under Order 7 Rule 11 application is in the nature of defence raised by the defendant which cannot be considered insofar as an application under Order 7 Rule 11 is concerned.
7. Sri.
Prasanna.

V.R, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that in para 8 of the plaint, the plaintiff has categorically admitted that acquisition proceedings have been completed and it is contended by the plaintiff himself that due to the acquisition proceedings being completed,
Sri Kalappa vs Mr Syed Noor Rafiulla on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70610675/
3 defendant No.1 cannot interfere with the possession of the plaintiff.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This very statement was sufficient for the trial Court to have taken into consideration for rejection of the plaint on an application being filed under Order 7 Rule 11 of CPC since once acquisition is completed, the plaintiff would have no right, title or interest in the property.

This submission of NC:
2024:KHC:21183 Sri.Prasanna.V.R, is supported by Sri.P.V.Chandrashekhar, learned counsel for respondent No.1-KIADB.

He reiterates the reference to both para 8 of the plaint as also submits that acquisition proceedings have been completed the KIADB has taken possession and the plaintiff is not in possession of the property to maintain a suit for bare injunction.

8. Plaintiff/respondent No.1 though has entered appearance by way of caveat through a counsel,
none has been appearing for respondent No.1.
9.

Having heard the counsel for the petitioner and counsel for the respondents and having perused the papers, I am of the considered opinion that the plaint itself indicates that there is an acquisition proceeding which has been completed.
Once the acquisition proceeding is completed, the plaintiff herein would not have any subsisting right, title or interest in the property.

Insofar as the contention that the plaintiff is in possession, the plaintiff has not sought for any NC: 2024:KHC:21183 relief against KIADB or State of Karnataka, suitable remedy would be for such person to challenge the acquisition notification in a writ court as provided under law, a suit not being maintainable and suit being barred in respect of any such properties.

10. Such being the case, there being no challenge to the acquisition made, the suit being barred as regards the lands which had been acquired by the State for and on behalf of KIADB, the said averment in para 8 ought to have been properly construed by the trial Court and the plaint was required to be rejected on that ground.
This aspect not having been properly considered by the trial Court, I am of the considered opinion that the impugned order is required to be set-aside.
11. As such, the Civil Revision Petition is allowed.
The order dated 31.10.2023 on IA filed under Order 7 Rule 11 of CPC in O.S. No.430/2020 passed by the II Addl.
Civil Judge and JMFC,
Devanahalli is set-aside.
Consequently, IA filed under Order 7 Rule 11 of CPC NC: 2024:KHC:21183 is allowed.
The plaint in O.S. No.430/2020 is rejected.
